title: The Best Burr Coffee Grinders for Home (2026)
excerpt: Fresh, even grounds are the cheapest upgrade in coffee. Three burr grinders for three budgets, and how to choose.

body.p: If your coffee tastes flat or bitter, the grinder is usually to blame, not the beans or the machine. Ground coffee goes stale within minutes, and a cheap blade grinder smashes beans into a mix of dust and chunks that brew unevenly. A burr grinder crushes beans between two plates set a fixed distance apart, so every particle comes out close to the same size. That one change does more for your cup than almost anything else you can buy.

ul: Burrs, not blades. Conical or flat both work well at home.
Enough grind settings for your brew method. Drip and pour-over need medium, French press needs coarse, espresso needs very fine.
Easy cleaning. Removable hoppers and burrs make a monthly clean painless.
Low retention, meaning little old coffee stays trapped inside to mix with today's grounds.

body.h: Best overall: OXO Brew Conical Burr Grinder

body.p: The OXO Brew is the easiest good grinder to live with. It has 40 mm stainless steel conical burrs, 15 main settings with micro-adjustments in between, and a one-touch start button that remembers your last setting, so most mornings you just press and walk away. The 12 oz hopper is tinted to block UV light. It handles drip, pour-over and French press very well. For true espresso you'll want something more specialized, but for everything else it's the one we'd buy.

body.h: Best for coffee enthusiasts: Baratza Encore

body.p: The Encore is the grinder many coffee professionals point beginners to, and it has won awards from the Specialty Coffee Association. It offers 40 grind settings on 40 mm conical burrs made in Liechtenstein, with a simple on/off switch and a front pulse button. The bigger selling point is longevity: Baratza sells replacement parts and supports its grinders for years, so this can be the last entry-level grinder you buy.

body.h: Best budget burr grinder: Cuisinart Supreme Grind

body.p: If you're coming from a blade grinder and don't want to spend much, the Cuisinart DBM-8 is the classic step up. It uses flat stainless burrs with 18 settings from fine to extra-coarse, and its grind chamber holds enough for up to 32 cups. It's louder and a little messier than the OXO, but your coffee will still taste noticeably better than with a blade grinder.

body.h: Which grind size for which brewer?

ul: French press and cold brew: coarse, like sea salt.
Drip coffee maker: medium, like sand.
Espresso: fine, like powdered sugar. Most budget grinders struggle here.
Grind only what you need right before brewing.
Brush out the burrs and chute every few weeks.
Never wash burrs with water unless the manual says you can. Use a brush or grinder-cleaning tablets.
Keep beans in an airtight container, not in the hopper for days.
